A buyer starting from a simple-traffic-reporting need who is weighing whether one tool can also cover product-level behavior can compare PostHog's documented product breadth against Plausible's documented site/team-based pricing tiers.

rivals.name: Google Analytics (GA4)
rivals.why: Nearly every buyer already has GA4 installed for free and has to justify replacing or adding to it before paying for anything else.

rivals.name: Fathom Analytics
rivals.why: The closest head-to-head pick for a buyer who wants a flat-fee, cookieless, single-dashboard tool across multiple sites instead of Plausible's pageview-tiered pricing.

rivals.name: Simple Analytics
rivals.why: Shows up for buyers pushing privacy further than Plausible (no visitor identifiers at all) and who want a free tier before committing to a paid plan.

rivals.name: Matomo
rivals.why: Where a buyer who needs more depth than Plausible offers (funnels, segments, enterprise/GDPR self-hosting) looks when simple pageview counts stop being enough.

rivals.name: PostHog
rivals.why: The tab open when the buyer's problem is really product analytics (session-level behavior, feature usage) rather than simple traffic reporting, and they're weighing whether to use one tool for both.

rivals.name: Umami
rivals.why: The self-hosted, open-source script a technical buyer or developer spins up themselves on their own server instead of paying anyone, especially before they've decided analytics is worth a subscription.
